A strict spec-conformant verifier rejects an array-valued `iss`, while the vulnerable target accepts it because one array element equals the allowed issuer.\n\n## The trigger token\n\n```\niss: [\"https://valid-iss\", \"https://evil.example.com\"]\n```\n\ncarries a value the target's policy does **not** allow (`https://evil.example.com`) inside a value form (`iss` as an array) the target nonetheless accepts — precisely the weakness a strict verifier rejects.\n\n## Delivery\n\n`/workspace/out/poc.py` is a single-file, stdlib-only, deterministic construct-and-report tool:\n\n- Builds a fixed HS256 token signed with a runtime-generated secret, passed via `--key`.\n- Runs the binary exactly once and reports the binary's own JSON result in `observable.value` (parsed then re-serialized), with `error: null` and exit 0 whether the token is accepted or rejected.\n- Handles the failure paths separately (unstartable binary, timeout, no parseable output) without ever failing on a rejection.\n- Byte-identical across runs (fixed `exp` of `2100-01-01T00:00:00Z`).\n\nVerified against the primary binary: `{\"ok\":true,\"payload\":{\"iss\":[\"https://valid-iss\",\"https://evil.example.com\"],\"exp\":4102444800}}`, deterministic across repeated runs, and error/timeout paths behave correctly.","ttft_ms":4935,"type":"result","duration_ms":663363,"uuid":"a1c8ea70-2434-4650-8fe5-7343f3750abc","ttft_stream_ms":2866,"time_to_request_ms":45,"first_content_frame_ms":2866,"queued_turn_count":0}
